page: Amazon Web Services m8a.large is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R45 processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at up to 4.5 GHz without multithreading overhead. The compute architecture includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 8 MB L3 cache, backed by vector instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, along with SHA-NI and AES cryptographic acceleration.

Memory capacity is configured with 8.0 GB of high-frequency 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage solutions, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Accelerators are not present, with zero dedicated GPUs assigned to the configuration.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional single-threaded compute capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core execution (3778.58), Geekbench single-core score (2822.0), single-threaded gzip compression (41.54 GB/sec), and text processing. Conversely, multithreaded capacity is constrained by the two-core ceiling, resulting in average ratings across Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core suites, and lower percentiles for thread-heavy tasks such as software compilation and ray tracing. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 54.26 GB/sec for read and 34.84 GB/sec for write operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8a.large offers strong value for workloads bound primarily by single-thread frequency and modern instructions rather than broad parallel scaling or high memory capacity. The instance is suited for lightweight web serving, API gateways, microservices, small database operations, and development environments that benefit from high per-core execution speeds without requiring expansive memory pools or local storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.large is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R45 architecture. It provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs at speeds up to 4.5 GHz, supported by 8.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory at 4.0 GB per core. The instance has no bundled local storage and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Compute benchmarks show top-tier single-core performance, evidenced by high Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression scores, though overall multi-threaded throughput and memory-heavy benchmarks remain moderate due to the 2-core envelope. The instance delivers high single-thread efficiency for entry-level deployments. It is suited for web serving, microservices, small database workloads, and application backends requiring modern vector instructions and responsive per-core speeds.
